Swiss Tariff Cut on Generic Drugs Could Ease Cost Pressure at BMY's Swiss Plants

medium

Policy Event Date: 2025-12-18

Per the Federal Register notice, the U.S. is adjusting tariffs on Swiss and Liechtenstein-origin goods, explicitly including generic pharmaceuticals and their ingredients and chemical precursors. As Bristol-Myers Squibb's 10-K discloses, the company has significant manufacturing operations in Switzerland, meaning any tariff change on Swiss-origin pharmaceutical products could directly affect the cost or competitiveness of goods produced there. While this is a tariff decrease—generally a favorable development rather than a disruption risk—the direct overlap between the policy's scope (Swiss generic drugs and precursors) and BMY's disclosed Swiss manufacturing footprint makes this a relevant, monitorable link for cost and margin implications tied to Swiss-sourced production.

Policy source: US-Switzerland Tariff Cut on Generic Drugs Filing source: Bristol-Myers Squibb 10-K

US-EU tariff relief on generics could ease cost pressure at AbbVie's Irish plants

medium

Policy Event Date: 2025-09-25

Per the Federal Register notice dated 2025-09-25, the US is adjusting (decreasing) tariffs on EU-origin products including generic pharmaceuticals and their ingredients and chemical precursors, under the US-EU reciprocal framework. AbbVie's 10-K discloses significant manufacturing sites in Ireland (Clonshaugh, Cork, Sligo, and Westport), an EU member state, meaning goods produced at these facilities and shipped to the US would fall within the scope of this tariff adjustment. While AbbVie's filing does not specify which product lines at these Irish sites are generics versus branded/biologic products, the geographic overlap between the policy's EU-origin scope and AbbVie's disclosed Irish manufacturing footprint means any tariff decrease on generics and their precursors could reduce import cost pressure on cross-border shipments from these sites. Severity is rated medium because the policy itself is high-impact (a formal US government tariff action), but the filing's risk text does not explicitly confirm generic drug production at the named Irish locations, introducing some uncertainty about the direct financial materiality to AbbVie specifically.

Policy source: US-EU Framework Tariff Cut on Generic Drugs Filing source: AbbVie 10-K

US Tariff Action on Chinese Semiconductors Adds to AMAT's Existing China Exposure

high

Policy Event Date: 2025-12-29

The Federal Register notice describes a new US tariff action targeting semiconductors from China, starting at 0 percent and increasing over 18 months, in response to China's chip-sector policies and practices. This escalates the broader US-China trade friction around semiconductors. Applied Materials' 10-K already flags China as a key risk area, disclosing that US export controls restrict the sale of certain technologies to customers in China. While the policy snippet addresses tariffs on semiconductors rather than equipment exports specifically, both actions stem from the same underlying US-China semiconductor tension and target the same country. AMAT's filing shows the company is already operating under restrictive conditions tied to China, meaning any further escalation in US-China semiconductor policy—such as this new tariff action—adds incremental regulatory risk on top of the export control exposure AMAT has already disclosed. The high severity reflects both the policy's explicit high-severity rating and the fact that AMAT's own risk disclosures confirm a direct, ongoing dependency on the US-China semiconductor policy environment referenced in the notice.

Policy source: Section 301 China Semiconductor Tariff Action Filing source: Applied Materials 10-K

China Entity List Expansion Directly Hits AMAT's China Export Exposure

high

Policy Event Date: 2024-12-05

On 2024-12-05, the U.S. Federal Register added entities involved in advanced-node integrated circuit and semiconductor manufacturing item production/development to the Entity List, per the federalregister.gov policy notice — a high-severity export restriction targeting advanced logic chip supply chains in China. Just days later, Applied Materials' 10-K (filed 2024-12-13) explicitly discloses that its business is subject to 'export controls established by the United States government to restrict the sale of certain technologies to customers in China,' as AMAT's 10-K states. Since AMAT is a leading supplier of semiconductor manufacturing equipment, the very technology category targeted by this Entity List expansion overlaps directly with its disclosed China risk exposure. This is not a speculative or indirect linkage — the policy action and the filing's risk factor describe the same underlying vulnerability: AMAT's ability to sell manufacturing equipment/technology to Chinese customers tied to advanced chip production. Portfolio managers should treat this as a near-term risk to AMAT's China revenue stream, given the direct alignment between the newly restricted entities and AMAT's already-flagged regulatory exposure.

Policy source: BIS Entity List Expansion on Chip Firms Filing source: Applied Materials 10-K
